title: O Father, Though the Anxious Fear
description: O Father, Though the Anxious Fear in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 7, “The Sabbath of the Soul”, where the book credits them to Springfield Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Fa-ther, though the anx-ious fear May cloud to mor-row's way, No fear nor doubt shall en-ter here; All shall be Thine to day.

lines: O Father, though the anxious fear
No fear nor doubt shall enter here;
We will not bring divided hearts
Ye shall not dim the light that streams
Ye shall not violate this day,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
